utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please, though, of course we know the lady.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin, and Andres Vatter, case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now for the Defence counsel who we know well as well, but can we have the appearances for the needs of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President, good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: And the other Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Kubura, for today, Mr. Rodney Dixon. Mr. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic will be present again from tomorrow. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. After a pause of a number of days, we are going to resume our hearings, and the Chamber bids good afternoon to all those present, Madam Benjamin, the Defence counsel, the accused, and all the staff of this courtroom. Today, as you know, we will be hearing a witness. But before we do that, the Chamber would like to make a few points of clarification regarding some outstanding matters. It has been envisaged that we have the closing session for the Prosecution on the 22nd of July. We know that the Defence would prefer it to be on the 21st of July, but according to the current schedule, it is not possible to have a hearing on the 21st of July except if another sitting planned for the 21st of July in this courtroom is cancelled. If we're informed about that in due course, then we will have our sitting on the 21st of July, but we will let you know as soon as possible when this sitting will take place, whether it will be on the 21st or the 22nd of July. As for the next three days, that is, as of today, we will have another sitting tomorrow at 9.00. According to the schedule, we were supposed to sit in the afternoon. But it is possible to have the sitting in the morning at 9.00. And the third sitting for this week will be on Wednesday, again, at 9.00. Having said that, the Chamber, which studied the matter last week with respect to the weeks to come, it is our opinion that should there be a motion of acquittal pursuant to 98 bis, the Chamber in that case gives the Defence a time period of three weeks. That is, the Defence counsel will have until the 11th of August 2004 to produce this motion for judgement of acquittal pursuant to Rule 98 bis. And, of course, we know that the Court will be in recess during the month of August. For the Prosecution to respond to the motion of acquittal, they will also have a three-week period which means that the Prosecution should submit their filings not later than the 1st of September 2004. In the event that the Defence wishes to reply to the submissions of the Prosecution, the Defence will have a three-day time period for this response. Therefore, the deadline would be the 6th of September. The Chamber, once it receives the filings of the parties, will render a ruling not later than the 27th of September 2004. We felt that we needed at least three weeks to be able to render our ruling. Therefore, our ruling will be made not later than the 27th of September 2004. Following this stage of the proceedings, the trial would resume under Rule 65 ter, and the Defence would have to submit its list of witnesses and documents following our decision which should be rendered not later than the 27th of September, will have five days to prepare these lists which would bring us to the 1st of October when this sitting could be held as provided for by Rule 65 ter. Following that, the Pre-Defence Conference could be held on Friday, the 8th of October, and the first Defence witness would testify beginning on Monday, the 11th of October. So that would be the general framework with the dates indicated so that the parties can take all measures necessary. Regarding filings, of course, it is up to the Chamber to limit the number of pages. The Chamber allots each Defence team 25 pages per Defence, which would make it 50 pages in all for the Defence of the two accused. One of the Defence counsel may cede to the other Defence counsel a certain number of pages on the basis of their mutual agreement. But the total for both Defence teams must not exceed 50 pages. The Prosecution's filings will also be entitled to 50 pages on the outside. To make things quite clear, if the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic needs 35 or 40 pages, they will use 40 pages. And then the Defence of General Kubura will only have ten pages, or vice versa. It is up to you to come to a mutual agreement. But when we add up those two documents, they cannot exceed 50 pages. It is quite possible that many arguments may be used by both sides, and there is no need to repeat the same things twice, so you can come to an agreement about this. But the point is it mustn't exceed 50 pages. You know that there is general directive which says that these documents may not exceed 30 pages, but we feel that 25 is quite sufficient. So that is what the Chamber wished to tell you. At this stage, would either party have any observations to make? Madam Benjamin, for the Prosecution, do you have any observations to make regarding the schedule, the number of pages, or any other point at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Except to get some clarification for one issue, Mr. President, in that the Prosecution would be filing one document for both Defence. That's basically -- so that our 50 pages will take in both accused. Sorry. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Prosecution may respond to the two filings of the Defence in a single document, but you Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond may also respond in two documents. But both cannot exceed 50 pages altogether. I now turn to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence for General Hadzihasanovic has taken note of your directives, and we will fully abide by the deadlines. The Defence is able to inform Your Honours already that within the time limit, we will file a motion of acquittal under Rule 98 bis, and we also feel that all the deadlines are quite realistic, should a Defence case be presented. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, I can also confirm that we will file a motion for acquittal and that it will easily be accommodated within the time schedule set out by Your Honours. And certainly, we will easily fit our submissions into the 25-page limit. So no further observations other than that. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. So we've covered all the outstanding points. We can now move on to the proceedings proper. And I should like the Registrar to give instructions for a private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me check that there's no one in the public gallery. There shouldn't be anyone there. We must make sure there's no one in the public gallery. Otherwise, we need to bring down the blinds. Yes, that's what we're going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now back in open session as the logo for private session is no longer on the screen. Ms. Benjamin, we have one more witness who should be appearing on Wednesday. Is this witness available for the Trial Chamber? Could he come tomorrow? Is it necessary to wait until Wednesday to hear this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness comes in tomorrow at 11.00 a.m. And I think our session has been changed again back to 9.00. Perhaps if we were going to start at 2.15, we could have had this witness ready. But since this has gone back to 9.00 tomorrow morning, I'm afraid he wouldn't be able to. Because he comes in at 11.30 tomorrow morning. My apologies to the Trial Chamber for what has transpired today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness will be here at 11.00, and so you should be able to speak to the witness. And we could commence the hearing at 2.15. Naturally, to avoid having to have the witness here for two days, we could commence with his hearing. And I haven't had a look at my list, but how much time did you think you would need to examine this witness who was to appear on Wednesday but who could appear tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I don't think the Prosecution needs more than an hour, Mr. President. I do not anticipate that our examination-in-chief would be longer than an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, will the courtroom still be available tomorrow at 2.15? Do you think you could check that? But I will first ask Defence counsel whether sitting tomorrow in the afternoon would be a problem for them or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We were expecting the hearing to be tomorrow in the afternoon. We agreed to appear in the morning since that was a possibility. But as far as our cross-examination is concerned, we shouldn't require more than an hour. But the time at which the trial will start might be a problem for us because I don't know whether when my colleague mentioned the time at which the witness would be arriving, I don't know whether she was referring to his arrival at Schiphol or in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: He arrives at Schiphol at 11.30. In anticipation this witness would have gone on tomorrow, my proofing for this witness would have been 3.00 tomorrow afternoon. But in anticipation that this was going to start tomorrow afternoon, we were going to proof him anyway, try to get him here by 12.30, 1.00, so that I could have proofed him before I come in to continue the witness today. So I don't think there's going to be a problem. I think we can get him here by at least 12.30, have him proofed, and be ready for 2.15, if we can have a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But given that the Defence wants to see the witness, we could start at 3.00 p.m. Would that be suitable? How much time do you think you'll need in order to speak to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we didn't think it necessary to see the witness. And we are quite prepared to start at 2.15 or at 3.00, whatever is most suitable for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But this all depends on the Registry. Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay. Very well. The person in charge has confirmed that the courtroom will be available, so we will commence at 2.15 tomorrow. If there's any delay, you will inform us of the fact, and we will make the necessary arrangements. As we have a little time left at our disposal, I will now turn to the decision that we were going to render on the documents. It should be ready by Friday for sure. We'll have it filed with the Registry at the beginning of the afternoon. So you should then have our decision which is still being completed, but it has almost finished. And we will provide it officially on Friday. This should allow the Prosecution -- but this is something that the Prosecution has to inform us of. It depends on whether we'll have a courtroom available on the 21st. The legal officer has told me that Defence counsel prefer the 23rd. That's the last day. So I will give the floor to the Defence. There are three possibilities next week: We could have a hearing either on the 21st, the 22nd, or on the 23rd in the morning. I thought that you preferred, or you would have preferred the 21st, but now I'm told that it's the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the 23rd is what the other Defence team would like, then we agree to that date. As far as Mr. Hadzihasanovic's Defence counsel is concerned, we accept that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If I could clarify, we would prefer either the 21st or the 23rd. But there was simply a scheduling problem from our point of view with the 22nd. If it had to be the 22nd, of course, Your Honour, arrangements could be made to ensure that it did go ahead on the 22nd. But our submission was if it really didn't matter which day it was, then we would prefer the 21st if a courtroom was available. If a court was not available, then the 23rd, if that was acceptable for Your Honours' scheduling. It should only be a short hearing, I understand. So if it didn't matter which day it was, then either the 21st or the 23rd, depending on available courtrooms. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar has told me that it's not possible on the 21st for the time being. That is the situation today. But five minutes later, the courtroom might be available. Ms. Benjamin, the Defence suggests the 21st or the 23rd. But the hearing might not take very long since this hearing will deal with two elements. Officially, you have to provide the Registry with the documents that relate to our decision that will be rendered on Friday. These documents have to be provided so the Registrar can provide them with exhibit numbers. Naturally, there won't be any numbers for the exhibits that have been rejected. That will be the first stage of the hearing, but we should be able to deal with this quite quickly since the Judges have been working on the matter for a number of weeks now. Then the second stage will involve you informing us officially that you have concluded the presentation of your case. Ms. Benjamin, at this point in time, is the 23rd a problematic date for you or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the 23rd is a convenient date for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for the moment, it will be the 23rd. If the 21st is a possibility, we will inform you of this fact, and that will give us two additional days to work. That will give you two additional days to work on your motion for acquittal. So we will try to ensure that we have the hearing on the 23rd. But the hearing tomorrow will start at 2.15, which means that there won't be a hearing on Wednesday. Are there any other issues that either of the parties would like to raise? I'm turning to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there was one matter concerning nine outstanding documents which I believe my learned friend from the Prosecution was going to raise. Perhaps this might be a convenient time to do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as these documents are concerned, there is a slight problem that remains. And the Prosecution wanted to discuss the matter. Ms. Benjamin, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, it has been brought to the attention of the Prosecution that there are nine documents that have internal OTP numbers, but for some reason or other was never dealt with. So there's no Prosecution number, there's no contested document number, and the documents are not in the possession of anybody else but the Prosecution. We have reviewed the documents on the weekend, and it is our impression that they are not particularly relevant to our purpose. And as such, we wish to on the record withdraw the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you provide us with the numbers of these documents, if you have them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: At the bottom of -- this is page 1 of the list. They're not in numerical order, but they start from 961, and the internal number will be 961956948, 954, 955, 951, 963, 966, and 949. I think that they were with a bundle of documents that were withdrawn earlier on, but for some reason these eluded that bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Trial Chamber has understood this correctly, there's a series of documents on the table, and you just mentioned the numbers of these documents. These documents will be withdrawn. According to the transcript, we can see these numbers in the transcript. 961, 956, 948, 954, 955, 951, 963, 966, and 949. That's nine documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will grant your request. Ms. Benjamin, as far as certain documents, the translation of which is still on standby, are concerned, the legal officer mentioned certain documents, and we are awaiting the translation of these documents. At what stage are you? Because if we don't have these documents by Thursday at the latest, we won't be able to admit the documents into evidence. We won't be able to do this if we don't have the translations of the documents. The translations requested are not lengthy, but there are a few documents the translations of which are still not available. Could you provide us with some information about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm informed that the translations are almost completed, and the Prosecution intends to supply the Court with all outstanding documents, re-translations and otherwise, by Friday. So we are hoping and grateful for the extension to the 23rd, that by Monday we should have tied up all our documents and everything should be in order for the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Ms. Benjamin, the question is that -- or the problem is that as I said, the Trial Chamber will be rendering its written decision on Friday. And this means that for us, and believe me, we have examined each document individually, spent hundreds of hours, thousands of hours, even, on the documents, this means that if we don't have the documents on Thursday, not next week but on Thursday, if we don't have the documents on Thursday, we won't be able to admit them because our decision will be rendered without a doubt on Friday. So perhaps you should make an effort. You have 48 hours. We still have 48 hours available. And we shouldn't have any problems because of a few pages that are missing. After having examined, as I said, all of these documents and spent hundreds of hours on them, we realised that there are certain documents in B/C/S hadn't been translated into English. And it is these outstanding documents that we must have. Could you make an effort and ensure that by Thursday at the latest we have these outstanding documents. The other solution, but legally speaking I would think this would be going a bit far. It would involve rendering a decision without having admitted the documents, but we need the translations. Could we have them by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I think I will have to give the Court an undertaking that I will try to get it to you by Thursday. We are finishing early, and I will personally endeavour to look at them, see what else is to be done, and I would try to make a commitment to the Trial Chamber that I can have it to you by, latest, Thursday. Because Thursday is just one day before Friday. So I will try my very best to have it on Thursday in light of what has been just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because if I've understood this correctly, among these documents that haven't been translated, there are some unofficial documents that haven't been stamped or certified by the -- by CLSS. The Rules don't state that a translation has to be certified by CLSS. English and French are the two working languages, and if we have the translation in one of the languages, it's sufficient. It's not necessary to have the document translated by the CLSS translator who is not part of this. This could also -- have translated the document in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Much obliged, Mr. President, and I will seek to ensure that we have the documents on Thursday. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Ms. Benjamin. Thank you. I know that the question of documents has meant that both parties have had a lot of work to do. This work has almost been completed, and this is why a solution has to be found in relation to the few outstanding documents. But there is a substantial matter that has to be addressed here. In the future, if the Prosecution has documents in a language that isn't one of the Tribunal's working languages, the Prosecution has to ensure the documents are translated. And when there is an indictment that accompanies documents, the confirming Judge must have at his disposal all the documents translated into one of the working languages, that is to say either into English or into French. We don't want to have situations in which we have an indictment, documents, we have a pre-trial stage, the beginning of the trial, and then later on we realise that there are certain documents that haven't been translated. This really poses a problem. And one must be careful because it has to do with the rights of the Defence and the work of both of the parties and of the Judges. The Judges have to have translated documents at their disposal. If there are no other issues to raise, we will resume tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you. And I will see you all tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of July, 2004, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.30 p.m.,
